data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Software can be refactored more easily than physical gears, reducing the permanent cost of a wrong choice.","A custom software tracker can remain minimal, whereas a racing transmission is inherently complex."],"overturn_conditions":["If the 'engine' (research algorithm) changes its fundamental operating principles mid-experiment, requiring a total transmission rebuild.","If the team is only doing 'cruising' (observational studies) and never 'racing' (active control)."],"shared_structure":["Consumer gearboxes (existing tools) are designed for stability and broad use, not high-frequency shifting under load.","Racing transmissions (custom trackers) are built around the specific torque curve and shift logic of the engine (active learning loop).","Adapting a consumer gearbox for racing introduces lag and failure points (integration tax) that obscure the driver's control."],"source_memory_refs":["building a custom racing transmission vs adapting a consumer car gearbox"],"transfer_claims":["Just as a racer needs a transmission designed for control rather than comfort, an active learning researcher needs a tracker designed for causality rather than just logging.","The 'lag' in a mismatched gearbox corresponds to the latency in a hacked software feedback loop, invalidating the experiment."]},"claim":"A small research team should adopt an existing experiment tracker only if their workflow is purely observational; however, if the research involves active learning loops where the tracker must function as a real-time controller to modify experimental parameters, they must build a custom minimal tracker to avoid the 'integration tax' of hacking a passive tool into an active agent.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The team lacks the engineering bandwidth to maintain even a minimal custom state machine.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The active learning loop can be fully encapsulated in an external script that treats the existing tracker purely as a log, avoiding direct integration.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The research timeline is too short to justify the upfront cost of defining a custom schema before data collection begins.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Control Theory Boundary: Existing tools are architected as passive data sinks (observational), whereas active learning requires a closed-loop control system (causal). Forcing a passive architecture to perform active control introduces high-latency feedback and fragile 'hack' layers that obscure the causal chain between hypothesis and parameter adjustment. A custom builder enforces the causal model by making the control logic the primary schema, not an afterthought.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
